correctness.rationale: Every possible palindrome in a three-marker circle has 0, 1, 2, or 3 ones. The four exhaustive structural inventories give exact formulas including repeated-gap and zero-gap cases. Sorting the gaps yields four exhaustive orbit types; explicit integer parametrizations and parity decomposition reproduce every term of the rational generating function. Uniform lattice-point convergence on the 2-simplex and inclusion-exclusion prove the limiting law and mean. Actual standalone checker independently matched entire palindrome sets for 8,000 gap triples, GF coefficients for m<=50, and 230 explicitly enumerated necklaces up to n=17. These finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accessible Simpson (2014) abstract establishes a global circular-palindrome bound and near-sharp constructions, while the OEIS A247000 entry gives maxima over all binary necklaces. Neither those bounds nor their single maximizing representatives determine the full coefficient array A_{m,p}, the per-three-gap inventory, or the limiting law. Actual external and research-record searches for three-marker circular palindrome inventories and generating functions identified no covering statement. The full 2014 article was inaccessible; this leaves explicit historical-priority uncertainty, not a claim of exhaustive literature clearance.
residual_risks: Simpson (2014) full text is plausibly relevant but could not be read; its near-extremal lemma may contain partial or equivalent gap computations.
Other papers may encode the same distribution under fixed-content palindromic complexity terminology; absence of a search hit is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Simpson’s near-sharp three-marker examples make the entire sparse family a motivated natural object rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Formula (1) describes each inventory, formula (2) gives all all-length multiplicities for each possible palindrome count, and formula (3) gives the asymptotic typical behavior. These results address a distributional gap not answered by the known unrestricted extremal bound or a few examples. Exact coefficients alone would be insufficient; their interpretation as a complete structural census supports the value.
